tools.name: manage_blog_post
tools.description: Create, update, publish, and inspect HubSpot blog posts. One action per call. Read actions: GET_POST, GET_AUTHOR, LIST_BLOGS, LIST_BLOG_POSTS, LIST_TAGS, GET_BRAND_KIT. Write actions: CREATE, UPDATE, SET_AUTHOR, PUBLISH, UNPUBLISH. A blog post is rich text (an HTML body) plus metadata and tags, N...

action.description: Action to perform. One per call. READ actions (no side effects): "LIST_BLOGS": list the blogs (content groups) in this portal, each with its id and name. Call this when the user wants a blog post but hasn't said which blog; if the portal has more than one blog, ask the user which one before CREATE, then pass the chosen id as blogId. No other fields required. "LIST_BLOG_POSTS": list existing posts in this portal as compact summaries (contentId, title, state, blog name, author name, slug, and updated time). Use this when the user asks about existing posts or wants to edit one but does not know its contentId. Optionally pass blogId to scope the list to one blog; limit defaults to 10 and is capped at 25. "GET_POST": fetch a post's current title, HTML body, meta description, and tags (requires contentId). Call before any edit so you change only what the user asked. "GET_AUTHOR": look up a blog author by email address (requires email). Returns the author's id, name, and email. Use this when the user wants to assign a specific author to a post or needs to find an author's id. "LIST_TAGS": list the blog tags in this portal. Returns tag names and ids. Call this before setting tags on CREATE or UPDATE so you can reuse a fitting existing tag by its exact name (tags are matched by exact name, so a near-variant would create a duplicate); if none fit, ask the user before creating a new tag rather than inventing one. Optionally pass limit (defaults to 25, capped at 100). Requires blog-tags-read scope. "GET_BRAND_KIT": fetch the portal's primary brand kit (colors, fonts, logos). Call before creating or restyling a post so the HTML uses the customer's brand colors and fonts instead of arbitrary defaults. No other fields required. WRITE actions (mutate the SAME draft — issue them ONE AT A TIME, never in parallel): "SET_AUTHOR": assign a blog author to the post (requires contentId). Pass blogAuthorId to assign an existing author directly. Alternatively, pass email and authorName: if an author with that email already exists it is used, otherwise a new blog author is created with the given name and email and then assigned. "CREATE": create a NEW draft blog post (requires title and postBody as HTML; metaDescription and comma-separated tags recommended; optional blogId — omit only when the portal has a single blog, otherwise pass the user's chosen blogId, which CREATE lists and requires when the portal has more than one blog). The post is created as a DRAFT. MUST be preceded by a proposal card (call render_blog_post_ui directly with a "propose" target) and an explicit user confirmation IN CHAT. Returns contentId and editorUrl. If applying tags, call LIST_TAGS first and reuse existing tags; if none fit, ask the user before creating a new tag (see the tags field). "UPDATE": update the post's HTML body, title, meta description, and/or tags (requires contentId; set one or more of postBody, title, metaDescription, or tags — omitted fields are left unchanged; when tags is set it replaces the full tag list — call LIST_TAGS first and reuse existing tags, asking the user before creating any new tag). "PUBLISH": publish the post so it goes live (requires contentId). Publishing is a separate, explicit step — only call it when the user clearly asks to publish; otherwise leave the post as a draft for them to publish from the editor. To schedule the post for a future time instead of publishing now, also pass publishAt. "UNPUBLISH": revert a published post back to draft (requires contentId). The post is taken offline and returns to draft state. Only call when the user explicitly asks to unpublish, take down, or revert a post to draft.

contentId.description: Content ID of the blog post. Required for GET_POST, UPDATE, SET_AUTHOR, PUBLISH, and UNPUBLISH. Not used by CREATE (which returns a new id), LIST_BLOGS, LIST_BLOG_POSTS, LIST_TAGS, GET_AUTHOR, or GET_BRAND_KIT.

blogId.description: ID of the blog (content group). For CREATE, omit only when the portal has a single blog; when it has more than one you must pass the user's chosen blogId (CREATE lists the blogs and errors otherwise). For LIST_BLOG_POSTS, optionally pass it to return only posts in that blog. Use LIST_BLOGS to discover ids.

postBody.description:
The post's body as an HTML string — use

/

for subheadings and

for paragraphs. Required for CREATE. For UPDATE, set it to replace the body (omit to leave unchanged). Blog posts are authored as HTML, not as a module grid. For font or text-color changes, put the inline style directly on every affected text-bearing element (h2, h3, p, li, a, span, etc.), not only on a wrapping div: HubSpot template CSS can override inherited wrapper styles.

title.description: Post title (the post's H1 / browser title). Required for CREATE. For UPDATE, set it to change the title (omit to leave unchanged).

metaDescription.description: SEO meta description for search snippets (~140–160 chars). Recommended for CREATE. For UPDATE, set it to change the meta description (omit to leave unchanged).

tags.description: Comma-separated blog tag names to apply (e.g. "dogs, pets, family"). On CREATE, applies these tags to the new draft. On UPDATE, replaces the post's full tag list; omit this field to leave tags unchanged, or pass an empty string to remove all tags. Tags are matched to the portal's tags by EXACT name, so call action=LIST_TAGS first and reuse an existing tag's name verbatim when it fits — a near-variant (e.g. "Content Marketing" when the portal already has "Marketing") will not match and creates a separate duplicate tag. Reuse existing tags; if none fit, ask the user before creating a new one (see createNewTags) rather than inventing tags — and if they don't approve, leave tags off. Tags must already exist in the portal unless createNewTags=true is set. Whitespace around names is ignored, duplicate names are removed, and each tag name must be at most 50 characters.

createNewTags.description: Set to true to allow creating new tags that don't already exist in the portal. Defaults to false. Leave it false unless the user has approved a new tag (see the tag-reuse rule on the tags field), and set it to true only after they approve or explicitly ask for a new tag. Never set it just to get past a "tag does not exist" error — if the user hasn't approved a new tag, add no tags instead.

email.description: Email address of the blog author. Required for GET_AUTHOR. For SET_AUTHOR, pass this with authorName to find-or-create an author by email. Ignored for other actions.

blogAuthorId.description: ID of an existing blog author. Used by SET_AUTHOR to assign a known author directly. Mutually exclusive with the email+authorName path. Ignored for other actions.

authorName.description: Display name of the blog author. Used by SET_AUTHOR together with email: if no author exists for the given email a new one is created with this name. Ignored for other actions.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return for LIST_BLOGS, LIST_BLOG_POSTS, or LIST_TAGS. LIST_BLOG_POSTS defaults to 10 (capped at 25). LIST_TAGS defaults to 25 (capped at 100). Ignored for other actions.

publishAt.description: When to publish the post. Only used by PUBLISH; ignored for all other actions. Omit it to publish immediately. To schedule, pass an ISO-8601 date and time with a UTC offset, for example 2026-11-10T09:00:00-05:00. It must be in the future. Convert the time the user gave into their own timezone's offset before passing it, and confirm the date and time with the user first.

createdByAgent.description: Attribution label stamped on the blog post to identify which agent created it (e.g. "Content Agent"). Only used by CREATE; ignored for all other actions. Leave unset when not creating on behalf of an agent.

tools.name: manage_segment
tools.description: Create, edit, convert, delete, or restore a segment, add/remove its records, or change its exclusions. Set operation.type to an operation below; segments are identified by list ID. <mandatory_confirmation> This tool writes to the portal. Before calling it, you MUST show the user a summary of the ...

name.description: The name for the new segment. If the user has not explicitly provided a name, ask for one before calling this tool.

objectType.description:
Mandatory field specifying the ObjectType to create the segment for.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, and other documented HubSpot objects) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` (e.g. `p885186001_fleet_vehicles`) that you MUST obtain from `discover_hubspot_schema` before searching — do not construct or guess it.
A plausible standard-looking name (e.g. `products`) may actually resolve to a different standard object OR a custom object. When you are not certain a name is a standard type, treat it as non-standard and resolve it via `discover_hubspot_schema` first, then use the exact `typeName` it returns.

memberObjectIds.description: CRM record IDs to pre-populate a hand-picked segment. Leave empty to create an empty segment; use AddMembersOperation for large batches. Leave empty when filterExpression is set: a static segment with filters takes its members from the filter, not from hand-picked IDs.

description.description: Optional short, user-friendly description of what the segment represents.

filterExpression.description:
Optional filter whose matching records fill the segment once, when it is created; it never updates after that. Set it ONLY when the user describes WHO should be in the list and wants that membership frozen. Leave it UNSET for an empty or hand-picked list, and never pass a filter crafted to match no records. When speaking to the user, call this a "static segment with filters" that won't update, and never say STATIC, DYNAMIC or "snapshot". When the user wants a list that keeps up as records change, use CreateDynamicSegmentOperation instead. Don't write exclusions into it: to keep out another segment's members, specific records, unsubscribed or non-marketing contacts, or an email domain, use the exclusion fields.

    SQL-like filter expression defining segment membership.

    Property conditions compare the object's own properties and combine with AND, OR and parentheses: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, CONTAINS_ANY (...), STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, IN (...), IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, BETWEEN x AND y. Relative dates use NOW() or TODAY() with whole-day offsets only — DAYS or WEEKS, never MONTHS/QUARTERS/YEARS (write NOW() - 90 DAYS, not NOW() - 3 MONTHS). Dates compare at day granularity, and a date property never compares = or != against a relative time (use a fixed date like '2026-08-13', or a rolling window). Example: "lifecyclestage = 'customer' AND annualrevenue > 500000". Write a value's apostrophe as two single quotes — lastname = 'O''Brien' — never with a backslash, which does not escape it.

    A != or NOT IN condition matches only records that have a value for the property; records where it is empty are left out. Include them only when the user asks, by writing (p != v OR p IS NULL) — it is stored as one condition, the segments UI's "Include records where ... is empty" option, so it does not multiply like other ORs. For a property of an associated record, put that pair inside the one ASSOCIATION's braces — ASSOCIATION(...) { (p != v OR p IS NULL) } — never as two ASSOCIATIONs joined by OR. Never include them by default.

    To leave out records that match any of several combinations of conditions on two or more properties ("not any of: in Boston and a Lead; in Austin and a Customer; ..."): with up to three combinations, write the negation directly, NOT ((city = 'Boston' AND lifecyclestage = 'lead') OR ...); it is stored as != conditions with their usual handling of records with no value, so add nothing for those. With more, that multiplies too far to store, so it needs a helper: a segment of the records the combinations describe, excluded from the new segment. An exclusion keeps every other record, including ones with no value for those properties. Before creating anything, tell the user there are too many combinations to write as one filter, so you'll build a helper segment and exclude it, and ask whether to include records with no value for those properties (if the user already said, only confirm the helper segment). To leave them out, give the new segment p IS NOT NULL for each of those properties. A NOT over one property's values stays a single NOT IN (...).

    Keep the expression small. Before it is stored it is expanded into disjunctive normal form, so every OR multiplies: OR groups of widths w1, w2, ... produce w1 x w2 x ... branches, and every ANDed condition is copied into every branch. Branches x conditions per branch is the stored filter count, and it must stay under 250. Multiply the OR widths before writing: 8 ANDed conditions with two OR groups of 5 and 10 alternatives is 50 branches and 500 filters, already rejected. Every ASSOCIATION and NOT ASSOCIATION is copied into every branch too, and a segment holds at most 60 of those copies: one beside an OR of 30 alternatives is already 30. Several values of one property are one condition and do not multiply: p IN ('a', 'b') for exact values, p CONTAINS_ANY ('a', 'b') for substrings — never an OR of p = ... or of p CONTAINS .... To fit, write those as one condition, drop redundant ANDed conditions, put ORed conditions in a helper segment referenced with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or split the audience across more than one segment; never narrow, drop or truncate the user's alternatives. A number IN (...) is stored as one filter per number, so a list of record ids (hs_object_id IN (...)) counts once per id, and inside an ASSOCIATION each id is its own association copy. A few ids fit: contacts at three given companies are ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = <id>) { hs_object_id IN (101, 202, 303) }. Only when the ids would take the segment past either limit, seed them into a hand-picked static segment of their own object type with membersToAddToStaticList and reference it with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) } for associated records.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Beyond property conditions, exactly these filter forms exist; names and named arguments (name = value, never positional) are exact — no other functions or aliases. Notation: [x] is optional; a | b means exactly one. times counts occurrences (>=, <= or =); occurred bounds when (>, >=, < or <= with a date or NOW() offset); for a window between two dates give occurred twice, one lower and one upper bound, both dates: occurred >= '2025-09-01', occurred <= '2026-06-01'. Each is optional and they MAY be combined — except where a form states an EXCEPTION.
    - IN_LIST(list = 4521): member of another segment/list (id from searchSegments). The same filter keyed differently for workflows and imports: IN_LIST(workflow = '112233', [state = 'ENROLLED'|'ACTIVE'|'COMPLETED'|'GOAL']) (state defaults to ENROLLED, ever enrolled) or IN_LIST(import = '555') — no list argument in those forms.
    - FORM_SUBMISSION([form = '<guid>'], [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 90 DAYS]): submitted a form. Leave form out for any form, e.g. FORM_SUBMISSION(occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS) — one condition, never an OR of every form.
    - PAGE_VIEW(url = '<exact url>' | url_contains = '<substring>', [times >= 2 | occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]): visited a website page. EXCEPTION: at most ONE refinement — a count OR a window, never both. The product stores one page-view refinement (the lists UI disables the second field too), so "twice in the last 30 days" is not expressible: keep the refinement the request makes primary, or ask the user which to keep. Page visits are ALWAYS this form, never UNIFIED_EVENTS — an event-form page-visit segment cannot be edited in the list UI. Negate with NOT_PAGE_VIEW(...).
    - ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = 1) { industry = 'SAAS' }: has an associated record matching the braces; object is the associated record's object type id, association the numeric association type id between the two types, and the braces hold conditions on the associated record's properties. An ASSOCIATION body is conjunctive; OR inside its braces is rejected, but IN (...) inside them is fine. NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { condition } means NO associated record matches the condition, and it includes records with no associated record at all — "contacts with no closed-won deal" is NOT ASSOCIATION(object = '0-3', association = 4) { dealstage = 'closedwon' }, and "companies with no deals" is NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { hs_object_id IS NOT NULL }. Its braces take exactly ONE condition written as =, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL or IN_LIST (not a date or a range). To leave out records associated with something matching several conditions at once, build a segment of those associated records first and write NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) }. Never move the negation inside the braces: ASSOCIATION(...) { dealstage != 'closedwon' } means "has a deal that isn't closed won", a different audience. A segment read back may carry match = 'ALL', 'ANY_INCLUDE_EMPTY' or 'ALL_INCLUDE_EMPTY' on an ASSOCIATION (all / any associated records match, including records with none); keep it as read when you edit the segment.
    - UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = '4-123456', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]) { [conditions] }: performed an event. The braces hold conditions on the event's OWN properties — take their names from searchFilterInputs (kind EVENT_PROPERTY), never from the segment object's schema.
    - EMAIL_EVENT(email = '169452110', app = 113, level = 'EMAIL_API_CAMPAIGN_GROUP', event = 'OPEN', [url_contains = '<substring>'], [occurred > '2026-01-01']): engaged with one specific marketing email. event is one of OPEN, CLICK, DELIVERED, SENT, REPLIED, BOUNCE, UNSUBSCRIBED, SPAMREPORT, PRINT. email, app and level come together from ONE searchFilterInputs (kind EMAIL) row — never mix rows or invent them. url_contains is valid only with event = 'CLICK'. EXCEPTIONS: occurred takes a fixed date only (rolling NOW() windows are rejected), no times, and no NOT form. For recency across ANY email ("opened an email in the last 30 days"), use the contact's email-engagement properties (e.g. hs_email_last_open_date) instead.
    Negate any form except EMAIL_EVENT by prefixing NOT, e.g. NOT IN_LIST(list = 4521). All forms combine freely with property conditions.

DYNAMIC (filter-driven) segments are rejected: their membership is computed from their filter and cannot be emptied manually — change the filter via UpdateSegmentOperation instead.

Edit an existing segment's exclusion (suppression) settings by an add/remove delta: segments
 whose members to hold out, individual records to hold out, and, for contact segments, the
 unsubscriber, non-marketing-contact, and email-domain exclusion rules. Only what is named
 changes; every other exclusion carries forward. It does not change the segment's filter or any
 record.

listId.description: The list ID of the STATIC segment to add the members to. The user needs edit access to it. A DYNAMIC segment is refused, since its members come from its filter; the refusal lists what to offer the user instead.

sourceListId.description: The list ID of the segment whose current members to copy, found with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery. It may be DYNAMIC or STATIC, but must hold the same object type as the segment they are added to. Use this, not GetSegmentMembersQuery plus AddMembersOperation, to put one segment's members into another. To keep a segment's members OUT, exclude it with UpdateSegmentSuppressionOperation instead; to keep up with the source as it changes, filter on its membership instead.

copyEveryMember.description: Set true only when the user confirmed copying a large segment after membersCopy.status came back NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, or had already said to copy all of them however many there are. A plain request to add a segment's members is not that, so leave it false: the tool then copies nothing and asks for confirmation first when the segment is large.

anyOf.description:
Copy every current member of one segment into a STATIC segment, without listing their record IDs.
 A one-time copy: records that join the source later are not added.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment to convert, found with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery. It keeps this list ID, its name, filters and exclusions, so the emails, workflows and other segments that use it stay connected. That is why this, never a create operation followed by DeleteSegmentOperation, is how to freeze a segment or make one active: a rebuilt segment gets a new list ID, and nothing that used the old one is reconnected.

convertTo.description: The type to convert the segment to. STATIC freezes a DYNAMIC segment with the members it has now: it stops updating, and records can then be added or removed by hand. Do it when the user asks ("stop it updating", "make it static", "lock in who's in it now"). DYNAMIC makes a STATIC segment built from filters update automatically again ("make it active", "keep it up to date"); its members are then recalculated from its filters. A hand-picked STATIC segment has no filters, so it can't become DYNAMIC; the refusal says what to offer instead.

confirmedMembersChange.description: Set true only when converting to DYNAMIC and the user confirmed, after conversion.status came back NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, that the segment's members will be recalculated from its filters, so records added or removed by hand don't stay that way. Leave it false otherwise: a conversion to DYNAMIC then changes nothing and asks for that confirmation first.

anyOf.description:
Convert an existing segment between DYNAMIC (active) and STATIC in place. It keeps its list ID, so
 whatever uses it stays connected, which a new segment built to replace it would not.

name.description: The new folder's name, 1 to 99 characters. Create a folder only when the user asks for one. Folder names don't have to be unique: when other folders already have the name, the response lists them, so ask the user whether they meant one of those.

parentFolderId.description: The folder ID to create it inside, found with querySegments SearchSegmentFoldersQuery. Omit to create it at the top level.

anyOf.description:
Create a segment folder, at the top level or inside another folder. It changes no segment; file
 segments in it with MoveSegmentsToFolderOperation, or a create operation's folderId.

listIds.description: The list IDs of the segments to move, up to 50, found with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery.

folderId.description: The folder ID to move them into, found with querySegments SearchSegmentFoldersQuery or returned by CreateSegmentFolderOperation; never guess one. 0 takes them out of every folder, to the top level.

anyOf.description:
File existing segments in a folder, or take them out of every folder. A segment is in at most one
 folder, so moving it takes it out of the folder it was in.

operation.description: The segment operation to perform. Set type to CreateStaticSegmentOperation, CreateDynamicSegmentOperation, UpdateSegmentOperation, AddMembersOperation, or RemoveMembersOperation.

confirmationStatus.description: User confirmation for this write. Defaults to UNCONFIRMED; the write is rejected unless set to CONFIRMED (or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION) after the user approves.

tools.name: manage_social_posts
tools.description: <purpose>Create, update, or cancel a HubSpot social post.</purpose> <capabilities> action=CREATE: create a post (mode=DRAFT (default) | SCHEDULE | PUBLISH_NOW) on one channel. Requires channelId and content. action=UPDATE: edit, schedule, or publish a draft or scheduled post in place. Requires br...

action.description:
Action to perform.
"CREATE": create a post (see mode). Requires channelId and content.
"UPDATE": edit a scheduled/draft post. Requires broadcastGuid; only the fields you pass change.
A FAILED post can't be updated: re-create it with CREATE, or reschedule it in HubSpot from its hubspotUrl.
"CANCEL": cancel a scheduled post by moving it back to a draft (unschedules it; nothing is deleted). Requires broadcastGuid. Only SCHEDULED posts can be canceled.

mode.description:
Publishing mode.
"DRAFT" (CREATE default): save without scheduling. Not valid on UPDATE — use CANCEL to unschedule.
"SCHEDULE": schedule for publishAt, or the channel's optimal send time when publishAt is omitted.
On UPDATE this schedules a draft or reschedules a scheduled post.
"PUBLISH_NOW": publish immediately — always confirm with the user first.
Omit on UPDATE, with no publishAt, to edit fields without changing when the post publishes;
a publishAt alone means SCHEDULE.

channelId.description: Channel ID to post to (from get_social_channels). Required for CREATE.

broadcastGuid.description: Broadcast GUID of an existing post. Required for UPDATE and CANCEL. Find it with read_social_posts.

content.description: Post text. Required for CREATE. Optional for UPDATE — omit to leave the text unchanged.

title.description:
YouTube videos only: the video's title, which YouTube shows apart from content (the description).
At most 100 characters, without < or >; any other title is rejected, and line breaks become
spaces. Optional for CREATE and UPDATE; when omitted, a new video takes its file's title, and an
existing title is kept unless YouTube would reject it. Rejected on other networks.

mediaUrl.description:
HubSpot File Manager URL of one public image to attach. Optional for CREATE and UPDATE; on UPDATE
it replaces the post's current media. Images only; to attach video or several files, use fileIds
instead. Ignored when fileIds is set — pass only one of the two.

fileIds.description:
HubSpot File Manager file IDs of the images or video to attach, in display order.
No tool looks files up: ask the user for each file's ID, shown as "File ID" in the file's details
in HubSpot File Manager. Each file must be public.
Optional for CREATE and UPDATE; on UPDATE they replace the post's current media.
Takes precedence over mediaUrl (mediaUrl is ignored when this is set) — pass only one of the two.
Each network limits how many files a post can have; a rejected set comes back with the reasons.

publishAt.description:
Scheduled publish time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. "2026-06-10T10:00:00Z"); must be in the future.
Only with mode=SCHEDULE; rejected with DRAFT or PUBLISH_NOW. On UPDATE, a publishAt with no mode
also schedules the post at this time. Omit it with mode=SCHEDULE to apply the channel's optimal
send time.

<satisfied>User expresses gratitude or approval.</satisfied>

tools.name: query_segments
tools.description: Read-only lookups that support the manageSegment write operations. Set operation.type to: - SearchSegmentsQuery: find segments by name, optionally by object type, list type, or folder, for the list ID other operations take; each names its folder. With deleted=true it searches only deleted segment...

query.description: Free-text search matched against segment names. Omit to list segments.

objectType.description:
Optional ObjectType to restrict the search to segments of that type. Omit to search across all object types.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` obtained from `discover_hubspot_schema`.

listType.description: Optional list type filter: DYNAMIC to only return auto-updating ("active") segments, STATIC to only return static segments. Omit to return both.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging when a response has hasMore = true.

deleted.description: true to search only deleted segments (the lists app's Recently deleted view), newest deletion first, to find the list ID a RestoreSegmentOperation takes. Deleted segments never appear in a normal search.

folderId.description: Optional folder ID, found with SearchSegmentFoldersQuery, to only return segments filed directly in that folder, such as when the user asks what's in it. Combine with query to search inside it. Not used with deleted=true. Each result names the folder it's in either way.

anyOf.description:
Find existing segments by name, optionally scoped to one object type or list type. Returns the
 summaries (list ID, object type, name) needed to target the other operations, e.g. the list ID
 for AddMembersOperation or a delete. With deleted, searches deleted segments instead, for the
 list ID a RestoreSegmentOperation takes.

kind.description: What to look up: ASSOCIATION for the association type ids usable in an ASSOCIATION(object = ..., association = ...) filter, EVENT for the event type ids usable in a UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = ...) filter, EVENT_PROPERTY for the properties usable inside a UNIFIED_EVENTS body, FORM for form guids (FORM_SUBMISSION), WORKFLOW for workflow ids (IN_LIST(workflow = ...)), IMPORT for import ids (IN_LIST(import = ...)), EMAIL for the marketing email triple (EMAIL_EVENT(email = ..., app = ..., level = ...)).

objectType.description: For kind ASSOCIATION (required) and kind EVENT (optional): the ObjectType of the segment whose filter you are writing — a standard name like CONTACT, or a portal-prefixed custom type from `discover_hubspot_schema`. For kind EVENT_PROPERTY (required): the event type id returned by a kind EVENT result, e.g. '4-123456'. Ignored for other kinds.

query.description: Free-text filter matched against names and labels. Omit to list everything available.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging when a response has hasMore = true.

anyOf.description:
Look up the ids that segment filter expressions take as arguments — association type ids, event
 type ids, event properties, form guids, workflow/import ids, and marketing email triples. Users
 do not know these ids, so resolve them here rather than guessing; each result includes a
 ready-to-use filter fragment to paste into a filterExpression.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment to fetch.

includeUsage.description: true to also return usedBy: what uses this segment, such as other segments' filters and exclusions, workflows, emails and ads. Set it when the user asks where a segment is used, or before deleting one, since a segment that's in use can't be deleted until those uses are removed.

deleted.description: true to read a deleted segment, for example to see its filters before restoring it with RestoreSegmentOperation. A deleted segment is otherwise reported as not found.

anyOf.description:
Fetch one segment's details by list ID: its object type, list type, name, description, the filter
 expression it is saved with, its exclusions, and who can access it. Use it to inspect a segment
 before editing it, or to answer what a segment filters on or excludes. This reports the segment's
 definition, not its members — use GetSegmentMembersQuery to list the records inside it. With
 deleted, reads a deleted segment instead, for example to see its filters before a
 RestoreSegmentOperation.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment whose member records to list.

properties.description: Optional internal CRM property names to additionally return for each member. Every member always includes its record ID and display name; these values are returned on top of that. Omit to return only the record ID and display name.

limit.description: Maximum number of members to return in this page; page through larger segments with cursor.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; to fetch the next page, pass the exact nextCursor value returned by the previous call. This is an opaque continuation token, not a number of members to skip — do not compute or increment it yourself.

anyOf.description:
List the CRM records that are members of a segment, by its list ID. This is the only way to read
 the records inside a segment: membership is not a CRM property, so a filter search cannot
 reproduce it. Works for both STATIC and DYNAMIC segments. Paginated: pass the response's
 nextCursor back as cursor to page through large segments. Returns only the records (and
 properties) the user is allowed to see, so a page can hold fewer members than limit while hasMore
 is still true; keep paging.

objectType.description: The ObjectType to count matching records for, the same value CreateDynamicSegmentOperation takes: a standard CRM type such as CONTACT or COMPANY, or a portal-prefixed custom type (`p<portalId>_<name>`) obtained from `discover_hubspot_schema`; do not guess one.

filterExpression.description:
The filter whose matching records to count: the same expression you would give CreateDynamicSegmentOperation, so the count is what that segment would hold. Required; this never counts an object type unfiltered. Do not write exclusions into this filter: to keep out another segment's members, specific records, unsubscribed or non-marketing contacts, or an email domain, pass them in this query's exclusion fields, the same ones the create operation takes, so the segment is created with them in one call. Write such a condition here (NOT IN_LIST, hs_email_optout, hs_marketable_status, an email NOT CONTAINS) only when the user asks for it as a filter, e.g. "add a filter for contacts who are not in my VIP Customers list".

    SQL-like filter expression defining segment membership.

    Property conditions compare the object's own properties and combine with AND, OR and parentheses: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, CONTAINS_ANY (...), STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, IN (...), IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, BETWEEN x AND y. Relative dates use NOW() or TODAY() with whole-day offsets only — DAYS or WEEKS, never MONTHS/QUARTERS/YEARS (write NOW() - 90 DAYS, not NOW() - 3 MONTHS). Dates compare at day granularity, and a date property never compares = or != against a relative time (use a fixed date like '2026-08-13', or a rolling window). Example: "lifecyclestage = 'customer' AND annualrevenue > 500000". Write a value's apostrophe as two single quotes — lastname = 'O''Brien' — never with a backslash, which does not escape it.

    A != or NOT IN condition matches only records that have a value for the property; records where it is empty are left out. Include them only when the user asks, by writing (p != v OR p IS NULL) — it is stored as one condition, the segments UI's "Include records where ... is empty" option, so it does not multiply like other ORs. For a property of an associated record, put that pair inside the one ASSOCIATION's braces — ASSOCIATION(...) { (p != v OR p IS NULL) } — never as two ASSOCIATIONs joined by OR. Never include them by default.

    To leave out records that match any of several combinations of conditions on two or more properties ("not any of: in Boston and a Lead; in Austin and a Customer; ..."): with up to three combinations, write the negation directly, NOT ((city = 'Boston' AND lifecyclestage = 'lead') OR ...); it is stored as != conditions with their usual handling of records with no value, so add nothing for those. With more, that multiplies too far to store, so it needs a helper: a segment of the records the combinations describe, excluded from the new segment. An exclusion keeps every other record, including ones with no value for those properties. Before creating anything, tell the user there are too many combinations to write as one filter, so you'll build a helper segment and exclude it, and ask whether to include records with no value for those properties (if the user already said, only confirm the helper segment). To leave them out, give the new segment p IS NOT NULL for each of those properties. A NOT over one property's values stays a single NOT IN (...).

    Keep the expression small. Before it is stored it is expanded into disjunctive normal form, so every OR multiplies: OR groups of widths w1, w2, ... produce w1 x w2 x ... branches, and every ANDed condition is copied into every branch. Branches x conditions per branch is the stored filter count, and it must stay under 250. Multiply the OR widths before writing: 8 ANDed conditions with two OR groups of 5 and 10 alternatives is 50 branches and 500 filters, already rejected. Every ASSOCIATION and NOT ASSOCIATION is copied into every branch too, and a segment holds at most 60 of those copies: one beside an OR of 30 alternatives is already 30. Several values of one property are one condition and do not multiply: p IN ('a', 'b') for exact values, p CONTAINS_ANY ('a', 'b') for substrings — never an OR of p = ... or of p CONTAINS .... To fit, write those as one condition, drop redundant ANDed conditions, put ORed conditions in a helper segment referenced with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or split the audience across more than one segment; never narrow, drop or truncate the user's alternatives. A number IN (...) is stored as one filter per number, so a list of record ids (hs_object_id IN (...)) counts once per id, and inside an ASSOCIATION each id is its own association copy. A few ids fit: contacts at three given companies are ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = <id>) { hs_object_id IN (101, 202, 303) }. Only when the ids would take the segment past either limit, seed them into a hand-picked static segment of their own object type with membersToAddToStaticList and reference it with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) } for associated records.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Beyond property conditions, exactly these filter forms exist; names and named arguments (name = value, never positional) are exact — no other functions or aliases. Notation: [x] is optional; a | b means exactly one. times counts occurrences (>=, <= or =); occurred bounds when (>, >=, < or <= with a date or NOW() offset); for a window between two dates give occurred twice, one lower and one upper bound, both dates: occurred >= '2025-09-01', occurred <= '2026-06-01'. Each is optional and they MAY be combined — except where a form states an EXCEPTION.
    - IN_LIST(list = 4521): member of another segment/list (id from searchSegments). The same filter keyed differently for workflows and imports: IN_LIST(workflow = '112233', [state = 'ENROLLED'|'ACTIVE'|'COMPLETED'|'GOAL']) (state defaults to ENROLLED, ever enrolled) or IN_LIST(import = '555') — no list argument in those forms.
    - FORM_SUBMISSION([form = '<guid>'], [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 90 DAYS]): submitted a form. Leave form out for any form, e.g. FORM_SUBMISSION(occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS) — one condition, never an OR of every form.
    - PAGE_VIEW(url = '<exact url>' | url_contains = '<substring>', [times >= 2 | occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]): visited a website page. EXCEPTION: at most ONE refinement — a count OR a window, never both. The product stores one page-view refinement (the lists UI disables the second field too), so "twice in the last 30 days" is not expressible: keep the refinement the request makes primary, or ask the user which to keep. Page visits are ALWAYS this form, never UNIFIED_EVENTS — an event-form page-visit segment cannot be edited in the list UI. Negate with NOT_PAGE_VIEW(...).
    - ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = 1) { industry = 'SAAS' }: has an associated record matching the braces; object is the associated record's object type id, association the numeric association type id between the two types, and the braces hold conditions on the associated record's properties. An ASSOCIATION body is conjunctive; OR inside its braces is rejected, but IN (...) inside them is fine. NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { condition } means NO associated record matches the condition, and it includes records with no associated record at all — "contacts with no closed-won deal" is NOT ASSOCIATION(object = '0-3', association = 4) { dealstage = 'closedwon' }, and "companies with no deals" is NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { hs_object_id IS NOT NULL }. Its braces take exactly ONE condition written as =, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL or IN_LIST (not a date or a range). To leave out records associated with something matching several conditions at once, build a segment of those associated records first and write NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) }. Never move the negation inside the braces: ASSOCIATION(...) { dealstage != 'closedwon' } means "has a deal that isn't closed won", a different audience. A segment read back may carry match = 'ALL', 'ANY_INCLUDE_EMPTY' or 'ALL_INCLUDE_EMPTY' on an ASSOCIATION (all / any associated records match, including records with none); keep it as read when you edit the segment.
    - UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = '4-123456', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]) { [conditions] }: performed an event. The braces hold conditions on the event's OWN properties — take their names from searchFilterInputs (kind EVENT_PROPERTY), never from the segment object's schema.
    - EMAIL_EVENT(email = '169452110', app = 113, level = 'EMAIL_API_CAMPAIGN_GROUP', event = 'OPEN', [url_contains = '<substring>'], [occurred > '2026-01-01']): engaged with one specific marketing email. event is one of OPEN, CLICK, DELIVERED, SENT, REPLIED, BOUNCE, UNSUBSCRIBED, SPAMREPORT, PRINT. email, app and level come together from ONE searchFilterInputs (kind EMAIL) row — never mix rows or invent them. url_contains is valid only with event = 'CLICK'. EXCEPTIONS: occurred takes a fixed date only (rolling NOW() windows are rejected), no times, and no NOT form. For recency across ANY email ("opened an email in the last 30 days"), use the contact's email-engagement properties (e.g. hs_email_last_open_date) instead.
    Negate any form except EMAIL_EVENT by prefixing NOT, e.g. NOT IN_LIST(list = 4521). All forms combine freely with property conditions.

    Sourcing ids — users do not know these ids; look them up, never invent one (a guessed id creates a segment that silently filters on the wrong thing): list ids from searchSegments; association type ids, event type ids, event property names, form guids, workflow ids, import ids and email triples from searchFilterInputs (kind ASSOCIATION, EVENT, EVENT_PROPERTY, FORM, WORKFLOW, IMPORT or EMAIL), whose results include ready-to-use filter fragments.

includeSampleMembers.description: Set true ONLY when the user wants to see examples of the matching records, not just how many there are. The result's sampleMembers then holds a few matching records by display name (a sample, never the whole audience). Leave false (the default) for a plain count; it skips an extra record lookup.

sampleProperties.description: Internal CRM property names of the object type to also return on each sampleMembers entry (e.g. 'industry', 'country'). Providing any implies includeSampleMembers. Leave empty to return sample members by name only.

countRecordsWithNoValue.description: Set true ONLY when the user asks how many records a != or NOT IN condition leaves out because they have no value for its property, e.g. "would including contacts with no company name make a difference?". The result's recordsWithNoValue then gives, per such condition, how many more records including them would add (0 means none). A condition on a date or inside an event filter can't include them and is not listed. Leave false (the default) otherwise; never set it on your own to decide whether to bring empty values up.

excludedSegmentIds.description: Optional: list IDs of segments whose members the segment will EXCLUDE, so the count leaves them out. Source them with SearchSegmentsQuery. When the user asks for a not-in-list FILTER instead, put the NOT IN_LIST condition in filterExpression and leave this empty.

excludedRecordIds.description: Optional: record IDs of the segment's own object type that the segment will EXCLUDE. At most 200.

excludeUnsubscribers.description: Set true when the segment will exclude unsubscribed contacts (default false). Contact segments only.

excludeNonMarketingContacts.description: Set true when the segment will exclude non-marketing contacts (default false). Contact segments only.

excludedEmailDomains.description: Optional: email domains whose contacts the segment will exclude. Contact segments only.

previewToken.description: Only when repeating a preview that failed with PREVIEW_STILL_RUNNING, including when the user later asks you to check it again: the previewToken from that error, copied exactly. Send it with the same objectType, filterExpression and exclusions to keep waiting on that same count instead of starting it over; the count keeps running in the background. Leave it empty (the default) for a new or changed preview; a token that doesn't match the query is ignored and the count starts from scratch.

anyOf.description:
Count how many records of an object type currently match a filter, without creating or saving
 anything, optionally leaving out the records the segment's exclusions would. Use it when the user
 asks how many records match, or wants a segment's size before it is saved; when the user simply
 asks for a segment, create it directly with CreateDynamicSegmentOperation.

query.description: Text the folder's name contains, ignoring case. Omit to list every folder. Folders belong to the account, so everyone sees the same ones. Folder names don't have to be unique: tell same-named folders apart by path. When no folder matches, say so and offer to create it with manageSegment CreateSegmentFolderOperation; never file segments in a different folder.

limit.description: Maximum number of folders to return.

anyOf.description:
Find the account's segment folders by name, each with its path through its parents, for the
 folder ID that SearchSegmentsQuery, MoveSegmentsToFolderOperation, and the create operations take.

operation.description: The read to perform. Set operation.type to SearchSegmentsQuery (find segments by name) or SearchFilterInputsQuery (resolve the ids used in filter expressions).

tools.name: read_campaign_data
tools.description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "read_campaign_data" and follow it; it contains the required parameter details and examples for each operation. Reads campaign data using one of four operations selected by the `operation` field. GET_ANALYTICS: engagement metri...

operation.description: Required. The operation to perform: GET_ANALYTICS, GET_ASSET_METRICS, GET_CONTACTS, or GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. The campaign's numeric CRM object ID (hs_object_id), greater than 0. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

requestedData.description: Required. The type of analytics data to retrieve. Only METRICS is supported — use it for engagement data (sessions, new contacts, influenced contacts). For revenue or attribution data, use getCampaignAttributionReports instead.

startDate.description: Optional start of the date range in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be provided together with endDate or both omitted. If omitted, defaults to the campaign's configured start date or up to 3 years ago.

endDate.description: Optional end of the date range in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be provided together with startDate or both omitted. If omitted, defaults to the campaign's configured end date or today.

attributionModel.description: Ignored. REVENUE_ATTRIBUTION is no longer supported — use getCampaignAttributionReports for revenue and attribution data.

requests.description: Required: List of analytics requests to process. Each entry is a full CampaignAnalyticsRequest. Maximum 20 requests per batch.

analyticsRequest.description: Analytics request data. Required when operation is GET_ANALYTICS.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. The campaign's numeric CRM object ID (hs_object_id), greater than 0. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

assetType.description: Required. Call readCampaignData with operation=GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES to get the exact portal-specific list of valid types (including custom objects) before using this field. For portal custom objects, pass the fully-qualified name (e.g. p12345_my_custom_object) as returned by GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES. If an invalid value is provided, the error will list the currently valid types.

crmObjectIds.description: Optional list of CRM object IDs to scope metrics to specific assets. When omitted or empty, metrics are returned for all assets of the given assetType associated with the campaign.

startDate.description: Optional start of the date range in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be provided together with endDate, or both omitted.

tools.name: read_social_posts
tools.description: <purpose>Read the HubSpot Social calendar: draft, scheduled, published, and failed posts managed in HubSpot. Networks: FACEBOOK, INSTAGRAM, LINKEDIN, TIKTOK, TWITTER (X), YOUTUBE.</purpose> <returns>posts [{broadcastGuid, source, network, channelId, channelName, status, publishAt, createdAt, hubs...

include.description:
Extra fields to return on each post. CONTENT adds the post text (content) and a YouTube video's
title (title). Pass it to read, quote, or compare what posts say, and always before editing a
post's text or title; leave it out for schedules, gaps, and counts.

broadcastGuids.description:
Look up these posts by broadcast GUID, e.g. to read a draft before editing it. Covers any
status the calendar shows; blog auto-publish posts (until they publish), AI suggestions, and
posts HubSpot is still processing read as not found.

statuses.description:
Filter by lifecycle status. Omit (or pass empty) for the default calendar view:
PUBLISHED + SCHEDULED + DRAFT together. A query search adds FAILED, and broadcastGuids has no
status filter.
Note: PUBLISHED here means posts published through HubSpot. For posts published directly on the
network, and for engagement, use get_social_post_analytics.

channelIds.description:
Filter by channel. An array of channel IDs; a post on any of them matches.
Omit (or pass empty) to read every channel you have access to. An ID you can't read is rejected.
get_social_channels lists the IDs.

networks.description:
Only posts on channels of these networks, e.g. [LINKEDIN], with no get_social_channels call
needed. Omit (or pass empty) for every network. With channelIds, a post's channel must match both.

query.description:
Only posts whose text has every word of this query, in any order, ignoring case, e.g.
"black friday". Words match whole words, not plurals or other forms, except the last word,
which also matches longer words it starts ("webinar" finds "webinars"). A hashtag is one word:
"black friday" misses "#BlackFriday", so also try "blackfriday". Use it to find posts on a
topic instead of reading every post's content.

startDate.description:
Start of the date range to read (inclusive), on scheduled/publish time, as an ISO-8601 date
("2026-08-01") or datetime ("2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"). A date with no time is interpreted as the
start of that day in UTC. Omit for no lower bound.

endDate.description:
End of the date range to read (inclusive), as an ISO-8601 date ("2026-08-31") or datetime
("2026-08-31T23:59:59Z"). A date with no time covers through the end of that day in UTC.
Omit for no upper bound.

limit.description: Max number of posts to return. Defaults to 10. Must be between 1 and 50.

offset.description: Number of posts to skip before returning results, for paging beyond limit. Defaults to 0. Must be >= 0.

tools.name: search_crm_objects
tools.description: Searches and retrieves CRM records from HubSpot by filters, associations, and criteria. Returns actual records, not field definitions (use search_properties to discover fields, discover_hubspot_schema to discover object types). Returns: id, requested properties, urlTemplate, total (match count fo...

objectType.description:
Mandatory field specifying the ObjectType to search for objects for.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, and other documented HubSpot objects) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` (e.g. `p885186001_fleet_vehicles`) that you MUST obtain from `discover_hubspot_schema` before searching — do not construct or guess it.
A plausible standard-looking name (e.g. `products`) may actually resolve to a different standard object OR a custom object. When you are not certain a name is a standard type, treat it as non-standard and resolve it via `discover_hubspot_schema` first, then use the exact `typeName` it returns.

query.description:
Optional text to search for within the default searchable properties of the specified object type.
Uses simple text matching (contains)
Each object type has different searchable properties.
contacts - firstname, lastname, email, phone, company),
companies - name, website, domain, phone),
deals - dealname, pipeline, dealstage, description, dealtype)
ticket - subject, content, hs_pipeline_stage, hs_ticket_category, hs_ticket_id)

[Important] Common stop words (e.g., "the", "a", "of", "and", "in") may not be indexed for some object types. If a query returns no results, retry by removing stop words or using property filters instead of free-text search.

Max length - 200 chars

properties.description: Optional list of property names to include in results. Returns default set if empty. Specify the minimum set of properties needed for the task for best results. Leave it empty only if you explicitly need to discover the full default property set.

propertyName.description: The name of the property to sort by

sorts.description: Optional sorting rules for results. Only one sort rule can be applied

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Max: 200, Default: 100

propertyName.description:
Specify the name of the Crm Object Property to filter on.

DO NOT use the pseudo-property `associations.{objectType}` or `associated_{objectType}` for associations.

You can use the following properties to filter by the number of associated records:

Tickets - hs_num_associated_companies
Companies - num_associated_contacts, num_associated_deals
Contacts - num_associated_deals
Deals - num_associated_contacts

operator.description:
Filter operator:
  EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, BETWEEN, IN, NOT_IN, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN
Usage:
  No additional parameters required for HAS_PROPERTY and NOT_HAS_PROPERTY

value.description: Value parameter for single-value operators (EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN)

highValue.description: High value for range-based operators like BETWEEN

values.description: Set of values for multi-value operators like IN and NOT_IN

items.description:
Represents a filter condition for CRM object searches.
 Filters specify criteria that property values must meet to be included in search results.
 The available operators are defined in {@link PropertyFilterOperator}.

filters.description: Set of filters in this group. All filters combined with logical ANDThe filter is used with associatedWith for AND logic in the same FilterGroup.

objectType.description:
Object type to find associations with.

Example: "companies" to find records associated with a company

operator.description:
Operator for association filtering:
- EQUAL/NOT_EQUAL: Associated with the specified object.
- IN/NOT_IN: Associated with any of the specified objects.

objectIds.description:
DEPRECATED: Use objectIdValues instead.
List of object IDs as strings to filter by.
If both objectIds and objectIdValues are provided, objectIdValues takes precedence.
Valid IDs are string representations of positive longs (e.g., '123', '456').

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. ["123"]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. ["123", "456", "789"]

objectIdValues.description:
List of object IDs to filter by.

At least one valid object ID must be provided.
Each object ID greater than 0.
Maximum of 100 object IDs allowed per association filter.

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. [123]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. [123, 456, 789]

associatedWith.description:
Association filters for finding records related to specific objects (e.g., "contacts for company X").

Within a single FilterGroup, all association filters are combined with AND logic.
Association filters are also ANDed with any property filters in the same FilterGroup.

Examples:
- Find contacts associated with company 123:
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]}]

- Find contacts associated with company 123 OR 456 (use IN operator):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "IN", "objectIdValues": [123, 456]}]

- Find records associated with BOTH company 123 AND contact 456 (multiple filters):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]},
   {"objectType": "contacts", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [456]}]

- To search for company A OR company B, use separate FilterGroups (FilterGroups are ORed together).

items.description:
Represents a group of filters that are logically connected with AND operators.
 Multiple filter groups in a search request are combined with OR operators.

filterGroups.description:
* The filter groups that define the search criteria.
 * Filters that match ALL of several conditions (AND logic) should be put in the same filterGroup.
 * Filters that match AT LEAST ONE of several conditions (OR logic) should be put in a separate filterGroup.

userIntent.description:
The original intent or goal the user was trying to accomplish.
Set to "<unchanged>" if the intent has already been submitted and hasn't changed.
Use generic or anonymized references instead of specific names, emails, or other PII.
Replace specific names with generalized references:
- Company/Partner names: "Bluleadz partner" → "partner A"
- Deal names: "Tesla deal" → "deal A"
- Customer names: "Acme Corp customer" → "company X"
Important: Avoid adding extraneous information other than what the user provides in the current chat.
Maximum 40 words.

satisfaction.description:
The user's satisfaction during the conversation.
  Set to DISSATISFIED when the user struggled with a feature, mentioned an unmet need or showed dissatisfaction.
  <dissatisfied_signals>
  - User provides explicit correction: "No, I meant...", "Actually, I want..."
  - User repeats query with different phrasing
  - User states something is wrong: "That's wrong", "That's not right"
  - User clarifies because agent misunderstood
  </dissatisfied_signals>
  Set to SATISFIED when the user expresses satisfaction, gratitude, or approval.
  Set to NEUTRAL when the conversation flowed smoothly without strong emotional signals.

chatInsights.description:
Insights about the chat including user intent and satisfaction level.
IMPORTANT: MUST be provided for all scenarios.
